metrics.name: Return on Equity
metrics.description: Net income over average shareholder equity. Net income is the shared reported-cost `fin.net_income`, after statement `tax_expense`. A same-period, unannualized decimal return. The denominator is the average of the opening balance (the prior period's close) and the closing balance, so the first period of a model is unavailable. Unavailable when an input is missing or the average is zero or negative; a loss stays negative. Rolled up by recomputing from the coarser period's earnings and its own opening and closing balances.

The denominator is the average of the opening balance (the prior period's close) and the closing balance, so the first period of a model is unavailable. metrics.name: Return on Invested Capital
metrics.description: EBIT less operating tax over average operating invested capital. EBIT is the shared reported-cost `fin.ebit`. `operating_tax` is the explicit operating tax expense before financing effects, a separate input from statement `tax_expense`; a credit is negative and raises the numerator. `operating_invested_capital` is the explicit period-end operating assets less non-interest-bearing operating liabilities, including required operating cash and excluding excess cash and nonoperating assets, in the same scope and currency as EBIT. A same-period, unannualized decimal return. The denominator is the average of the opening balance (the prior period's close) and the closing balance, so the first period of a model is unavailable. Unavailable when an input is missing or the average is zero or negative; a loss stays negative. Rolled up by recomputing from the coarser period's earnings and its own opening and closing balances.

metrics.name: Return on Capital Employed
metrics.description: EBIT over average capital employed, total assets less current liabilities at each period end. EBIT is the shared reported-cost `fin.ebit`. A same-period, unannualized decimal return. The denominator is the average of the opening balance (the prior period's close) and the closing balance, so the first period of a model is unavailable. Unavailable when an input is missing or the average is zero or negative; a loss stays negative. Rolled up by recomputing from the coarser period's earnings and its own opening and closing balances.
